conflicts.description: Interview evidence uses a broad observed 'head movement' category and reports an association, whereas technical papers report axis-specific algorithm error. These statistics answer different questions.
conflicts.risk: Treating estimator MAE as a behavior threshold, or treating broad head movement as equivalent to all three Euler-axis p95 metrics.
conflicts.required_review: Separate construct validity from measurement accuracy; validate each Face-Fit axis on the actual 5 FPS pipeline.

conflicts.description: The positive meta-analytic association for 'head movement' does not show whether more, less, or a particular kind of movement is favorable for any axis.
conflicts.risk: An absolute p95 penalty would assume a monotonic direction that the source does not establish.
conflicts.required_review: Obtain cue definitions and effect directions from included primary studies; collect Face-Fit-specific ratings.

conflicts.description: Eye contact is directly coded in interview research, while public-speaking systems sometimes use head orientation as a proxy. Face-Fit does not measure ocular gaze.
conflicts.risk: Equating camera-facing head pose with eye contact can misclassify users who move their eyes independently of their head or look at an on-screen interviewer window.
conflicts.required_review: Define camera/screen geometry and either implement validated gaze measurement or label the feature strictly as head orientation.

conflicts.description: The closest interview result uses 2D optical flow in real interviews, while public-speaking studies use Kinect/full-body multimodal features in laboratory or virtual-audience tasks.
conflicts.risk: Pooling these sources would hide task, sensor, population, and feature-definition differences.
conflicts.required_review: Do not average results. Validate shoulder-center velocity separately on asynchronous interview video.

conflicts.description: Optical-flow features, weighted motion energy, and multi-camera 3D millimeter errors cannot be converted into normalized landmark velocity per second.
conflicts.risk: Invented conversion factors would create an unsupported numerical threshold.
conflicts.required_review: Use only Face-Fit pipeline units in a new labeled dataset; retain literature values as non-convertible context.

conflicts.description: The 2D validation papers test gait joint angles or shoulder flexion, not the angle of the line joining left and right shoulders.
conflicts.risk: An anatomical label containing 'shoulder' may be mistaken for direct validation of shoulder tilt.
conflicts.required_review: Perform a dedicated left-right shoulder-line validation against manual labels or calibrated reference measurements.

conflicts.description: Reported head-pose errors differ across Hopenet, FSA-Net, OpenFace, MediaPipe, 3DDFA, and benchmark/clinical datasets; pitch and yaw are generally less stable than roll in the controlled MediaPipe study.
conflicts.risk: Selecting the smallest published error would ignore algorithm and dataset mismatch.
conflicts.required_review: Benchmark the exact Face-Fit PnP implementation, MediaPipe version, resolution, and 5 FPS sampling against labeled videos.

conflicts.description: Sources span employed managers, Swiss student-heavy real interviews, MIT mock interviews, US crowdworker monologues, and heterogeneous meta-analytic samples.
conflicts.risk: A universal threshold may create construct-irrelevant group and context differences.
conflicts.required_review: Pre-register subgroup, device, language, accommodation, and fairness analyses in Face-Fit's own target population.

conflicts.description: Behavioral interview evidence does not determine engineering availability cutoffs. Availability reflects detector/capture quality rather than interview performance.
conflicts.risk: Scoring missingness as poor posture could penalize lighting, camera, occlusion, assistive technology, or model bias.
conflicts.required_review: Keep quality gating separate from behavioral scoring and validate it with failure-mode and fairness testing.

conflicts.description: The scoping review found heterogeneous, frequently author-developed human-rating instruments, while automated public-speaking studies use sensor-specific composites.
conflicts.risk: Frequency of posture or head-movement labels across rubrics could be mistaken for construct validity of a specific kinematic metric.
conflicts.required_review: Develop and validate a Face-Fit-specific observational rubric before relating kinematics to expert judgments.
